subject: Prior on scaling parameter to shrink towards zero

messages.author: ef76f4ec1ca10943
messages.subject: Prior on scaling parameter to shrink towards zero
parts:
Hi,

I would like to fit a preferential model such as:

~ ... + f(field_pp, model=...) + f(field_mark_copypp, copy = "spde_pp" , fixed = F, hyper = list( beta=... )) + f( field_mark2, model=...)

where beta shrinks towards zero. In other words, I want the model to somehow neglect "field_mark_copypp" when the data is not really preferentially sampled, i.e. "field_pp" does not resemble the actual field of the marks.

So far I have unsuccesfuly tried these two:
  •  gaussian prior --> list(prior = 'gaussian', param = c(0, .051))
  • and a pc.prior --> list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prior",  param = c(0, 1e-9),
        initial = c(0, 0))
Both the mark and the pp use log links. May this be why the above dont work?
Any suggestions?

Cheers,
iosu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior on scaling parameter to shrink towards zero
parts:
Thanks for your fast reply Finn! Yes, it is an error sorry.it should be "field_pp" as well.

Sorry for not explaining well enough my problem. By "dont work" I meant that when I draw a random sample (homogeneous pp), field_pp is not a flat function because it draws information from the marks when fitting the shared field  field_mark_copypp. As a results field_mark_copypp + field_mark2 does resemble the marks function, but the Poin Pattern field (field_pp ) is far from realistic.

My though was that, if I were able to put a strong prior on the scaling parameter to shrink towards zero, field_pp could be realistic (konstant) and have a minimal impact on the marks function. And consequentely, field_mark2 alone would resemble the marks function.

cheers,
Iosu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior on scaling parameter to shrink towards zero
parts:
Hi
I see. That _might_ work if the model for the marks was otherwise perfect, but information flows both ways, and if it (where “it” is probability theory…) thinks the field component would be useful for modelling the marks, that could in  practice override the prior.  This is a very tricky identifiability problem.

Finn
